title: THE UNTOLD STORY OF GOLIATH
paragraphs: The Giant Was Bigger Than You Think
Most people think they know the story.

A giant.
A shepherd boy.
A stone.
A victory.
But the real story is far more disturbing.
Because Goliath was never the biggest giant on that battlefield.
And fear still walks among us today.
The tragedy is that millions of believers know David's victory, but they have never understood Goliath's purpose.
Because Goliath was not merely a warrior.
He was a weapon of psychological warfare.
He was designed to make God's people forget who God was.
In private battles nobody talks about.
The story begins long before David ever picked up a stone.
The story begins with a nation that forgot how to trust.
"And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them."
The Hebrew word for valley here is:
And isn't that where most of us live?
Between what God said and what we currently see.
The valley is where giants appear.
Goliath Was a Monster of a Man
"And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath..."
The Hebrew word translated "champion" is fascinating.
The one who stood between two armies and declared:
Just as David represented more than himself.
This battle was never merely personal.
The traditional Hebrew text describes Goliath as:
Whether slightly shorter or exactly that height, the point remains unchanged.
His armor alone weighed approximately 125 pounds.
Satan has always specialized in appearances.
The enemy wants problems to look larger than God's promises.
He wants sickness to look permanent.
The giant's first weapon was not his spear.
The Forty-Day Attack Nobody Talks About
"And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days."
Until Israel began believing the giant's version of reality.
The voice repeats itself until it sounds true.
Many believers are not losing battles because the giant is stronger.
They are losing because they have listened too long.
"When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid."
The Hebrew phrase implies being shattered internally.
Because fear had already defeated him before the battle ever started.
Many people believe courage means not feeling fear.
Biblically, courage means obeying God while fear is screaming.
David did not have less fear.
David Saw Something Nobody Else Saw
When David arrived, everybody saw a giant.
He did not identify Goliath by his size.
He identified him by his spiritual condition.
David saw a man disconnected from the living God.
The Secret Nobody Knew About David
David's confidence did not begin in public.
David learned dependence where nobody was watching.
The greatest victories in your life will rarely begin on public stages.
The shepherd ran toward the giant.
The Hebrew text paints a picture of urgency.
He did not wait for ideal conditions.
The earth shook beneath a warrior everyone thought could never be defeated.
A prophetic picture of Jesus Christ.
Jesus fought a battle others could not fight.
And just as David defeated the giant on behalf of Israel...
Christ defeated sin, death, and hell on behalf of humanity.
The Greek word used in the New Testament for Savior is:
The victory of Jesus was not merely an example.
He fought where we could not.
He conquered what we could not conquer.
He carried what we could not carry.
And because He rose again, the greatest giant humanity ever faced has already fallen.
The Giant Standing In Front Of You
Maybe your giant is not nine feet tall.
Maybe it's a secret sin nobody knows.
Maybe it's the voice in your head telling you you'll never change.
The same God who stood with David still reigns.
The same Christ who defeated death still saves.
The same Holy Spirit still empowers believers.
But it is not larger than God.
Somebody reading this has spent months listening to the giant.
Someone else may need your story today.
The giant that terrified an entire nation became the testimony of a shepherd who trusted God.
